The smile's tilt and wings on SPXW same-day options

    1. The four tests and their verdicts

    Two claims (A1, A3) and two questions (A2, A4) were written before either feature was computed on any day. Each is judged by the rank correlation between the feature at the start of a window and the result of that window, set against what the time of day alone produces.
    A claim says a higher rank goes with a higher result. It is held if the rank correlation is above the time of day alone with p ≤ 0.05 on both half-years. A question claims no direction. It is a finding if p ≤ 0.05 on both half-years, on the same side.

    Feature
    Result, for the charts and bucket tables

    2. Predictive: the feature at the start, the result of the 30 minutes that follow

    Both features are read from the chain of the window's first minute, so both are known before the trade. Each enters as its rank against its own last 20 trading days at the same time of day. The four buckets are the quarters of that rank, with fixed cut lines at 0.25, 0.50 and 0.75.

    3. Before any feature: what each structure earned, and what the spread cost

    All windows, no feature used. The first six rows hedge every minute at no cost. The last row is the desk's one-sixth band with every cost paid.

    The cost of the spread, for one window and for a day of twelve windows

    4. The features themselves

    The median and the middle half of each feature at each time of day. The tilt is in volatility points: 1.0 means the put wing is one volatility point dearer than the call wing.
